topic: How much tremor may be left at the pen tip for words to be readable (EXP-E13, study F simulation, HW1)
citation: This study's simulation (readable/): model HW1, study R's real-input library and reader; the curve fitted on R's tuning split, frozen, confirmed once on R's test split
task_or_setup: The Rev J nose driven by perfect knowledge made imperfect three ways: (a) the tremor scaled (amplitude error), (b) the perfect estimate delayed 5.2-25 ms (lag error), (c) perfect + band-limited noise (f0 +- 2 Hz); severe (1.72 mm) and moderate (0.24 mm) classes; words read by TrOCR base (literal) against R's tip-tremor measure; log-logistic fit with a writer bootstrap
participants_or_bench: Simulated (real recorded inputs: UNIPEN hpb2 writers, UCI PD tip tremor, Zenodo ET hand tremor; study R's tuning and test splits)
comparator: Ordinary pen; the same notes without tremor
key_quantitative_findings: Tuning split: residual for +2 words over the ordinary pen (DEC-055's words line) 0.65 [0.56-0.70] mm; for 80 % of the tremor-free words 0.25 [0.20-0.30] mm; within 1 word of the clean notes 0.19 [0.15-0.22] mm (ordinary pen 0.76, clean 8.49 words of 10). Test split: +2 words at 0.55 [0.47-0.64] mm; 80 % at 0.26 [0.22-0.31] mm; at the level aimed at the tuning +2 residual the test gain was 1.98 [1.44-2.61] words
units_and_conditions: mm (peak = sqrt(2) x RMS of the major axis of ink - intended in contact, f0 +- 2 Hz); words of 10; SIMULATION
limitations: Simulation; composed inputs (healthy writers' notes + patients' tremor); AI reader stands in for people (EXP-R03); 5 tuning and 9 test writers; residuals are idealised shapes; R's tremor waveforms keep only f0 +- 2 Hz and 2 f0 +- 2 Hz
relevance_to_design: The target any tremor estimator must reach at the severe class
transferability_reason: Simulation with real inputs and an AI reader, not a measurement of people or of a pen
design_implication: An estimator must leave no more than the +2-words residual at the tip at the severe class to meet DEC-055's words line; the test split confirms the order of magnitude

topic: Per-writer calibration of the tremor estimator's authority gate on the user's own clean writing (EXP-E11, REQ-CTRL-016; study F simulation, HW1; information only)
citation: This study's simulation (readable/e11.py): rule chosen on R's tuning split (each tuning note calibrated on its writer's other note), applied once to R's test writers (calibrated on a different note of the same writer)
task_or_setup: Study E's frozen ai2 TCN + soft size gate (D1), the real-data TCN + gate (D2), the listening AKF + confidence gate (D3); the gate's opening threshold set from the quantile of the estimate's size on the writer's own clean note (grid of 24 rules)
participants_or_bench: Simulated (real recorded inputs: UNIPEN hpb2 writers, UCI PD tip tremor, Zenodo ET hand tremor; study R's tuning and test splits)
comparator: The same designs with study E's frozen gates
key_quantitative_findings: D1|cal: clean writing moved mean 5.4 um, worst writer 19.1 um (0 over 50 um); severe words gain -0.22 [-0.55-0.06]; severe tip tremor x ordinary 0.75 [0.67-0.84]; D2|cal: clean writing moved mean 2.3 um, worst writer 18.9 um (0 over 50 um); severe words gain 0.11 [-0.10-0.36]; severe tip tremor x ordinary 0.62 [0.56-0.70]; D1|frozen: clean writing moved mean 68.2 um, worst writer 493.0 um (1 over 50 um); severe words gain -0.05 [-0.15-0.00]; severe tip tremor x ordinary 0.69 [0.63-0.75]; D2|frozen: clean writing moved mean 2.5 um, worst writer 18.9 um (0 over 50 um); severe words gain 0.05 [-0.21-0.31]; severe tip tremor x ordinary 0.60 [0.54-0.65]
units_and_conditions: um RMS on the notes without tremor; words of 10; SIMULATION
limitations: Study E has already seen the test split: a feasibility check only; one clean calibration note per writer; a severe-tremor user has no tremor-free writing to calibrate on; EXP-R01 shadow-mode data are needed
relevance_to_design: REQ-CTRL-016 (per-user gates) and DEC-061's revisit trigger
transferability_reason: Simulation with real inputs and an AI reader, not a measurement of people or of a pen
design_implication: Calibrate the gate on the user's own writing and only ever raise its threshold: it kept every simulated test writer within 50 um for both networks; it adds no tremor removal, so no words are gained (docs/readable_target.md s5)

topic: Where the gap between causal tremor estimators and perfect knowledge lies: prediction, sensing or separating tremor from writing (study F simulation, HW1)
citation: This study's simulation and calculation (readable/gap.py) on R's tuning and test splits
task_or_setup: Severe class: perfect knowledge; a causal linear (AR) predictor on the true tremor over the pen's horizon (4.9 ms); estimators fed the pen's sensor streams of the tremor alone; the same estimators on tremor + writing; each estimate drives the nose on the full case; residuals mapped to words through the frozen E13 curve
participants_or_bench: Simulated (real recorded inputs: UNIPEN hpb2 writers, UCI PD tip tremor, Zenodo ET hand tremor; study R's tuning and test splits)
key_quantitative_findings: Test split, tip tremor (words via the curve): fir_raw: oracle 0.03 mm (8.4 words) -> pred_ar_imu 0.03 mm (8.4 words) -> fir_trem_raw 0.29 mm (6.3 words) -> fir_full_raw 0.72 mm (2.9 words) | ai2tcn_gated: oracle 0.03 mm (8.4 words) -> pred_ar_imu 0.03 mm (8.4 words) -> ai2tcn_trem_gated 1.05 mm (1.5 words) -> ai2tcn_full_gated 1.12 mm (1.2 words) | net_gated: oracle 0.03 mm (8.4 words) -> pred_ar_imu 0.03 mm (8.4 words) -> net_trem_gated 0.89 mm (1.9 words) -> net_full_gated 0.97 mm (1.7 words)
units_and_conditions: mm (R's measure); words of 10 via the curve (CALC); SIMULATION
limitations: R's tremor waveforms are band-limited by construction (a broadband check on raw ET recordings is reported); the linear filter is one estimator design; composed inputs
relevance_to_design: Whether to invest in prediction or in sensing and separation
transferability_reason: Simulation with real inputs and an AI reader, not a measurement of people or of a pen
design_implication: Invest in separating tremor from writing first and in a drift-free position reference in the tremor band second; prediction and latency need no investment (docs/readable_target.md s7)

topic: Predicting real tremor over the pen's 4.9 ms horizon is not the limit (study F calculation)
citation: This study's calculation (readable/gap.py) on the true handle tremor of R's tuning cases and on raw Zenodo ET tuning recordings (broadband check)
evidence_class: numerical simulation and calculation on recorded data
task_or_setup: Direct least-squares AR predictor (Delta and order chosen on the tuning split, cross-fitted by fold): newest sample 1.52 ms old (IMU path), prediction to the servo delay (3.39 ms); hold (no prediction) as comparator; horizons 3.4-10 ms
participants_or_bench: Simulated (real recorded inputs: UNIPEN hpb2 writers, UCI PD tip tremor, Zenodo ET hand tremor; study R's tuning and test splits)
key_quantitative_findings: Cross-fitted in-band residual on the severe tuning cases: AR 2.7 um, hold 326.1 um (at 1.72 mm); on 11 raw ET recordings made displacement in a broad band (f0 - 2 Hz to 20 Hz) the AR's in-band error at 4.9 ms is 0.11 % of the tremor, 16.1 % with no prediction
units_and_conditions: um (R's measure on the prediction error); CALC
limitations: Band-limited library waveforms; broadband check on ET hand recordings only (PD tip data are pixel-quantised)
relevance_to_design: The prediction horizon of the Rev J/Rev K command path
transferability_reason: Simulation with real inputs and an AI reader, not a measurement of people or of a pen
design_implication: Prediction does not need investment; the estimate itself does

topic: Reach a nib needs for the readable target at the severe class (study F simulation, HW1; tuning split)
citation: This study's simulation (readable/reach.py): the Rev J nose with its usable travel limited to +-3, +-2, +-1.5 and +-1.0 mm, driven with perfect knowledge on R's tuning cases
task_or_setup: Severe class (1.72 mm), 20 tuning cases (5 writers, PD and ET); perfect knowledge and perfect knowledge scaled to the frozen +2-words residual; tip tremor (R's measure); words read for perfect knowledge at +-1.5 and +-1.0 mm
participants_or_bench: Simulated (real recorded inputs: UNIPEN hpb2 writers, UCI PD tip tremor, Zenodo ET hand tremor; study R's tuning and test splits)
comparator: The same runs with the +-6 mm Rev J nose
key_quantitative_findings: Perfect knowledge leaves at the tip: +-6 mm 0.02 [0.02-0.03] mm; +-3 mm 0.15 [0.11-0.19]; +-2 mm 0.43 [0.35-0.49]; +-1.5 mm 0.67 [0.59-0.74]; +-1.0 mm 1.00 [0.94-1.06]. Words read at +-1.5 mm 4.0 [3.3-4.6] of 10 (gain over the ordinary pen 3.2 [2.6-3.7]), at +-1.0 mm 2.2 [1.5-2.8] (gain 1.4 [0.8-1.9]): below DEC-055's +2 at +-1.0 mm. An estimate that leaves the +2 residual at full reach leaves 0.82 [0.77-0.86] mm at +-1.5 mm, 0.71 [0.69-0.73] at +-2 mm, 0.65 [0.65-0.66] at +-3 mm. The perfect-knowledge command in contact: 99th percentile of its 2-D magnitude 3.8 mm, above 1.0 mm 61 % of the time
limitations: The Rev J nose's mass and servo with its travel cut, not the B1 nib's own dynamics; tuning split only; one seed per case
relevance_to_design: DEC-050 / DEC-060 (the nib's reach) against the readable target
transferability_reason: Simulation with real inputs and an AI reader, not a measurement of people or of a pen
design_implication: At the severe class a +-1.0 mm nib cannot meet DEC-055's words line even with perfect knowledge; +-1.5 mm can with perfect knowledge; an estimator with its own error needs about +-2-3 mm (docs/readable_target.md s8)
